LanLine Communications needs to replace a legacy billing platform whose vendor is no longer operating. Tom’s engineers are keeping it alive, diverting skilled resources from billable customer work and creating continuity risk. The company needs a dependable platform for recurring billing, billable tickets, work orders, customer payments, technician activity, assets, and reporting. The goal is to begin running Rev.io in parallel with the current system by January 1, validate billing accuracy for roughly two to three months, and then complete the cutover without disrupting customers

Single Points of Failure across employee resources

- Monthly billing takes five to six days and requires Tom to collect paperwork desk-to-desk. - Technician notes contain acronyms and shorthand that must be rewritten for customers. - Incomplete work orders and weak process discipline cause revenue leakage; Tom previously uncovered about $8,000 per month in missed billing. - The unsupported legacy system consumes engineering time and creates operational risk. - Customers need a reliable portal for invoices and credit card/ACH payments. - LanLine lacks efficient tracking for technician travel, on-site time, assets, maintenance dates, and proactive replacement opportunities. - Staff adoption and data quality remain critical dependencies for any new platform.

Rev.io can reduce billing from nearly a week toward one day by automating recurring charges and moving ticket labor, parts, and approvals into a controlled billing workflow. Mobile time tracking, travel/on-site timers, customer alerts, and permission-based status flows can improve technician accountability and capture billable work. The customer portal modernizes invoice delivery and payment collection. Asset and scheduled-maintenance tracking can support proactive replacement recommendations for UPS batteries, drives, firewalls, and other equipment. Real-time dashboards, collections automation, branded invoices, parent-child billing, and QuickBooks integration provide better operational control while preserving accounting workflows. Revy can improve grammar and customer-facing notes when technicians provide usable source detail

Ben planned to fully exit Red Rover IT by year end, but former customers and team members asked to come back, so he is relaunching as a new hybrid MSP built around a small, tight customer base. He wants the new company on one simple, low-overhead platform for PSA and billing instead of rebuilding on the patchwork of ConnectWise, Autotask, Odoo and a bare-bones SkySwitch billing instance he has cycled through over the years.

Preparing for Rapid Growth

- Lost revenue: $300-$500/mo ($3.6K-$6K/yr) leaks from missed and uncharged services; onsite visits went unbilled. - Billing accuracy: Hand-keyed billing and manual ACH with no auto-matching let a $200 error go unnoticed for 3 months. - Admin time: Owner loses a full business day every month reconciling 30-50 invoices across 2 billing systems. - Customer experience: ~20 customers get separate IT, telecom and one-time invoices, causing confusion and missed payments. - Tool sprawl: 2 instances (~$600/mo) with ticketing that loses asset history and leaves tickets open after resolution.

Rev.io recovers $3.6K-$6K/yr in leaked revenue and gives Ben back a full day every month by putting billing, payments and service on one platform. Consolidating tools saves another ~$600-$700/mo while every customer gets a single accurate invoice.

Digital Transformation

TPG Security Tech needs a reliable way to schedule, track, and close out quoted field projects while keeping service work moving across multiple sites. Today, project schedules and progress rely on Google Calendar and manual updates; field notes and site documentation are hard to capture against the correct location and convert into accurate invoices. The company is still deciding what PSA/CRM operations tools to add around its recent QuickBooks Online rollout.

Digital Transformation

• Multi-day to multi-week projects are scheduled in Google Calendar; progress and hours against project budgets are assessed manually. • Field technicians need fast mobile/tablet access to site documents, photos, configurations, and service history; current workflows often rely on laptops or manual transcription. • Multi-site accounts make it easy to associate notes with the wrong location, driving invoice corrections and back-office follow-up. • Scope changes need to be priced, approved, and signed at the site without delaying work. • SIP-trunking activity does not reconcile automatically to QuickBooks Online; payment processing and collections also remain operational concerns.

Consolidate project/service scheduling, time capture, field notes and site records, quoting/change orders, and invoicing into a unified PSA workflow integrated with QuickBooks Online. Potential value: clearer project progress and hours vs. budget; more complete, site-specific billable records; less manual back-and-forth with accounting; faster field execution without a laptop; and documented on-site approval for scope changes. Adoption and total cost—including payment processing—must be validated before ROI can be claimed.

Copeland wants to grow without adding headcount at the same rate. Its seven-to-eight-person team supports roughly 3,000–4,000 NinjaOne seats, but ConnectWise creates rigid, click-heavy work across service, billing, reporting, collections, and account management. The platform costs about $30,000 per month and renews in mid-2027, creating a defined window to evaluate a replacement. Copeland needs an automation-first PSA that preserves its human-touch, agile operating style while improving scalability, visibility, and employee leverage.

Single Points of Failure across employee resources

- Monthly billing consumes 10–12 hours from a key employee due to WisePay, ConnectWise, and QuickBooks reconciliation. - Pax8 billing and contract data do not align reliably. - Collections are manual, and the bookkeeper lacks sufficient visibility. - BrightGauge reporting is static and requires manual exports and table maintenance. - Account managers manually log activities, time, and follow-ups after calls. - ConnectWise workflows are rigid, procedural, and poorly matched to Copeland’s culture. - Support and account management relationships have deteriorated. - Every additional capability requires another paid module. - Documentation/configuration integrations remain an evaluation concern

Rev.io can help Copeland scale its existing team through native AI, automation, and unified workflows. Revy can answer operational questions, summarize tickets, prepare QBRs, create records, capture notes, and schedule repeatable skills—while keeping actions permission-based and human-approved. Rev.io can reduce billing reconciliation by managing invoices, payments, credits, and reversals before pushing detail to QuickBooks. Native collections, Pax8 and NinjaOne integrations, ticketing, CRM, quoting, projects, mobile time capture, SQL-level analytics, and Signal & Send can replace manual work and paid add-ons. The strongest value case is reclaimed staff time, improved account coverage, faster decisions, and growth without proportional hiring

TransNexus, a long-standing Rev.io partner, is evaluating Rev.io as a potential billing customer to simplify Stripe-based invoicing and payments, reduce engineering involvement in billing, and support usage-based products and a new product launch. It needs a low-disruption transition and a defensible business case while balancing another internal project.

Single Points of Failure across employee resources

- About 500 customers receive over 1,000 monthly invoices across multiple products and accounts, creating confusion and duplicate-invoice issues. - Stripe fees deducted from deposits complicate reconciliation; customers manually initiate payments. - Tax calculation errors reportedly cost a few hundred dollars monthly. - Engineering handles billing tickets and Stripe administration. - Usage is priced across roughly seven tiers, with some annual true-ups. The existing automated disconnect integration must be preserved or replaced safely

Rev.io could consolidate or separate invoices as needed, provide a customer portal and autopay, automate collections, support usage feeds and improve QuickBooks Online reconciliation. SureTax can calculate address-based taxes; tax configuration and results still require validation. Separate processing-fee invoicing could simplify deposit reconciliation. Included ticketing, projects and quoting may provide additional value. Quantify labor, processing and tax benefits; do not assume savings until validated.

Broken Relationship with a Rev.io Competitor

- Halo does not flow cleanly from purchase order/sales order into project execution, budgets, assets, and cost tracking. - Field technicians lack a strong mobile workflow, causing notes and time to be entered in bulk later, which creates missed detail and inaccurate time capture. - Help desk and project work live in separate operational “worlds,” with limited cross-visibility and no unified calendar view. - Static billing misses dynamic changes like license count increases, overtime, and project time. - Reporting is weak enough that they rely on CloudRadial for client-facing reporting and previously used BrightGauge internally. - Procurement notifications and received-item workflows are not intuitive.

Rev.io can give Grey Matter a modern PSA built around AI, unified workflows, and operational visibility across service, projects, procurement, billing, reporting, and field work. Key value points include end-to-end project management, project billing, distributor integrations, mobile/geofenced technician workflows, AI-assisted reporting and dashboards, payment processing, and a permission-based model where core features are included rather than modular add-ons.

Schultz Technology is evaluating whether Rev.io can replace Cordial as the billing system across a mixed telecom stack that includes SkySwitch, CoreDial/Cordial, White Label carrier services, and Textable. Their current process creates billing, reconciliation, and operational gaps: payments land in QuickBooks Online as lump sums, service changes require updates in multiple systems, SMS usage is manually audited, and telecom tax/499 reporting still requires manual work.

Market or Product Expansion

- Cordial does not directly integrate with QuickBooks Online, creating lump-sum payment reconciliation with limited line-item visibility. - SMS/Textable usage is growing but still requires manual monthly audits and overage calculations. - Service changes must be updated separately in SkySwitch and Cordial, increasing missed-change risk. - Internal communication gaps can cause billing changes to be missed. - 499 reporting and telecom compliance reporting are manually handled from Cordial reports. - MRR is not yet confirmed, which limits pricing clarity.

Rev.io can consolidate billing across SkySwitch, CoreDial/Cordial, White Label, and Textable usage into one system, automate CDR imports and SMS overage rating, sync invoice/payment detail into QuickBooks Online, support Avalara and compliance reporting workflows, and automate collections. This reduces manual audits and reconciliation work while improving invoice accuracy, billing visibility, and financial controls. Longer term, Rev.io PSA/ticketing could also be positioned against ConnectWise for deeper billing-to-operations integration.

Cine Audio Visual is evaluating a modern operating platform because its core system has been in use since 2008, is expected to reach end-of-life, and lacks the project-management and progressive-billing capabilities the team now needs. The initiative must reduce fragmentation across integration projects, short-term rentals, field tracking, and accounting visibility without sacrificing Cine’s established order-centric workflow.

Digital Transformation

Legacy and fragmented operating systems: Cine’s core platform dates to 2008 and is expected to reach end-of-life; rentals are handled in a separate system that is also becoming less satisfactory. The buyer wants integration, rental, project, and financial workflows to operate more cohesively. Timing and continuity impact are not quantified. Manual project-cost tracking: Technicians record hours and materials in spreadsheets, and project status is tracked through email and direct communication. Entries can be missed, so leadership sees labor consumption and overruns reactively rather than continuously. The demo clarified that Cine charges fixed labor—for example, $2,000—but needs actual hours for project costing, not time-based billing. Realized losses remain unquantified. Progress and milestone billing limitations: The current system cannot directly invoice a percentage of a project, forcing workarounds. Cine uses structures such as 50/20/30, deposits, item-level charges, and phase-based progress billing.

If fit and adoption are validated, Cine could replace spreadsheet handoffs with direct project time capture, see budget consumption continuously, improve control over labor overruns, and move more consistently from quote through purchasing, execution, and milestone invoicing. Peter confirmed that time tracking and project visibility align with what the team is seeking, and he saw advantages in the updated flow.

The investment must demonstrate clear value through time savings, potential software consolidation, and improved billing and collections. Budget is a concern; Heather indicated that Mike’s initial reaction was that a purchase likely would not happen this year.⁠

Digital Transformation

- Disconnected operations: QuickBooks Desktop, Outlook scheduling, shared drives, scanned documents, photos, and manual work orders create fragmented job information. - Owner dependency: Mike remains heavily involved in project execution; limited infrastructure makes delegation difficult. - Manual quoting: Word-based proposals require data entry and product links. Heather wants more professional estimates with product details and supporting documentation. - Complex billing: Long-running construction projects require deposits and progress billing, while security customers require installation invoices followed by recurring charges. - Collections workload: An employee spends significant time managing aging balances. Payments are often pursued after installation instead of collected in the field. - Payment transition concerns: ASI wants to preserve automatic reconciliation and avoid repeatedly requesting customers’ payment information. - Prior implementation friction: D-Tools felt cumbersome because of QuickBooks accounting alignment and inventory data-entry requirements.

- Operational efficiency: Centralize customer records, job documentation, scheduling, time tracking, and project status to reduce administrative handoffs and information searches. - Greater delegation: Give staff access to job information and repeatable processes, reducing dependence on Mike for routine decisions. - More consistent quoting: Standardize professional proposals and e-signatures; evaluate replacing standalone DocuSign and PandaDoc subscriptions. - Improved cash flow: Support field payments, recurring billing, and automated collections to reduce follow-up work and payment delays. - Flexible accounting transition: Integrate with QuickBooks Desktop now, with the option to move to Online later. - Potential processing savings: Review merchant statements against ASI’s reported $30,000–$50,000 in monthly card volume and approximately 3% current processing rate. Constellation Dealership Software is evaluating a new voice / VoIP services initiative for its dealership customer base. The goal is to have billing, usage rating, telecom tax, compliance, payments, customer portal, and white-labeled invoicing in place before going live. Milad would ideally like the solution ready by year-end with roughly 10 customers live by the beginning of the year, though compliance timelines may push this into Q1.

Market or Product Expansion

They are still early in the evaluation and do not have a finalized billing, carrier, tax, compliance, or payment architecture. Milad has spoken with 40+ vendors and is comparing NetSapiens direct, SkySwitch, OIT, OneBill, DataGate, tax engines, and legal/compliance firms. Key concerns are telecom compliance, tax remittance, multi-carrier flexibility, white-labeled billing, external payment processing through Perseus Pay / Adyen, and AI usage billing. True prepaid wallet / top-up / suspension for AI usage is a gap that needs deeper validation.

Rev.io helps Constellation launch voice services faster and more safely by giving them a proven telecom billing and AR platform instead of building billing, tax, usage rating, and portal workflows from scratch. The value is reducing launch risk, supporting compliant billing, enabling white-labeled customer invoicing, supporting future multi-brand / reseller models, and giving them flexibility to work with multiple carriers instead of being locked into one provider ecosystem. Rev.io also gives them enterprise implementation support and long-term scalability if the voice initiative expands across Constellation companies.

E Squared is evaluating Rev.io because its current operating stack is fragmented across e-Sub, 360E, Foundation, Foundation Field Log, Teams/SharePoint, Asana, and SecuraTrac. The core business issue is too many disconnected platforms causing poor field-to-office communication, limited reporting visibility, techs working across multiple apps, and inventory spread across systems.

Broken Relationship with a Rev.io Competitor

- e-Sub handles field reports/time cards but only exports to Foundation via Excel/CSV. - 360E handles estimating/quoting and some project tracking but does not fully connect the business workflow. - Foundation is the accounting/payroll/dispatch source of truth but is complex and seat-limited. - Techs use multiple apps, creating friction and inconsistent field-to-office communication. - Reporting/analytics visibility is limited across service, projects, labor, inventory, and profitability. - Inventory tracking is spread across vans, warehouse, and separate systems. - Full GPS tracking is constrained by union concerns, so mileage/time tracking must be handled carefully. - They have evaluated several platforms already; ServiceTrade lacked project management and Building Ops was too large/complex.

Rev.io can create value by consolidating service desk, time tracking, quoting/proposals, project management, inventory, dispatch, reporting, and customer communication into one PSA workflow while still supporting Foundation through CSV exports/imports. The strongest value is reducing app fatigue for techs, improving field-to-office communication, giving leadership better real-time visibility, and creating cleaner quote-to-cash workflows tied to projects, labor, inventory, and accounting outputs

Single Points of Failure across employee resources

-Triple entry: QuickBooks quote → manually retyped Service Fusion estimate/work order → PDF of proposal stored; estimate notes swapped for job notes on conversion -Proposals: QuickBooks output "not very customer facing friendly"; needs ballpark quotes ("access control project, 13 doors, here's a price") with full itemization kept on the back end — his strongest reaction of the call -Change orders: contractor projects require original proposal + separately totaled change orders (QuickBooks contractor package does this today) — Rev.io gap; roadmap only Inventory: nothing electronic; Excel thresholds -Service contracts: contract customers aren't charged for post-install service calls — needs entitlement tracking; asked how recurring invoices are scheduled/grouped -Project profitability: no tracking today; project management module never reached on this call -GPS: no solution since OBD failure; Rev.io is app-based only (he asked about vehicle integration — answer is no)

-Kill the double entry: quote → ticket → invoice in one system; new API-based QuickBooks Desktop integration (web connector, no Transaction Pro) — no cloud migration required, which dissolves his internal cloud-vs-desktop stalemate -Customer-friendly proposals with per-section detail control + native e-sign — replaces the QuickBooks-proposal + AI-reformatter + Adobe patchwork; directly targets his net-new conversion problem -Electronic inventory (POs, serialization, reserve-from-ticket, asset lifecycle) — replaces Excel -Agreements with included-hours entitlements + automated recurring billing — his service contracts are "our big recurring struggle"; office manager reportedly spends 80–90% of time on billing -Email-to-ticket, drag-drop dispatch with calendar sync, offline mobile app, job costing per ticket

Alliance Systems Integrators is a 50-employee commercial security/integration business operating across Long Island and Massachusetts with disconnected tools and manual workflows. They use QuickBooks Desktop, Excel, Jitbit, Snappy, and a separate GoTrack GPS platform, none of which are well integrated. As the company has grown, legacy processes have not kept pace, causing billing leakage, inventory shrink, inaccurate time tracking, project-management friction, and significant administrative rework. They want to modernize before year-end and are also interested in moving from QuickBooks Desktop

Single Points of Failure across employee resources

- Inventory is manually tracked across 3 warehouses and 15 trucks, creating 18 inventory points with high error risk. - Estimated $150K in material with 8–10% shrink, or at least $15K/year lost. - Delayed or missed billing happens at least monthly; average sale is around $100K, with possible 5% leakage. - Snappy is basic and does not provide integrated GPS, time tracking, or inventory. - Jitbit handles work orders/help desk separately. - Excel is used for project management and RMR tracking. - Time tracking is only about 85% accurate and requires weekly manual review.

Rev.io can create value by consolidating ticketing, dispatch, mobile technician work, GPS/time tracking, inventory, project management, billing, RMR, payments, and QuickBooks workflows into one connected PSA. The hard ROI story includes reducing $15K/year in inventory shrink, preventing $5K/month billing leakage, eliminating roughly $800/week of manual checking, improving technician productivity, and replacing spreadsheet-driven operations with real-time workflows. The mobile app is especially compelling because Carly already likes the concept and their current field workflow is basic/manual.

LanLine Communications needs to replace a legacy billing platform whose vendor is no longer operating. Tom’s engineers are keeping it alive, diverting skilled resources from billable customer work and creating continuity risk. The company needs a dependable platform for recurring billing, billable tickets, work orders, customer payments, technician activity, assets, and reporting. The goal is to begin running Rev.io in parallel with the current system by January 1, validate billing accuracy for roughly two to three months, and then complete the cutover without disrupting customers

Single Points of Failure across employee resources

- Monthly billing takes five to six days and requires Tom to collect paperwork desk-to-desk. - Technician notes contain acronyms and shorthand that must be rewritten for customers. - Incomplete work orders and weak process discipline cause revenue leakage; Tom previously uncovered about $8,000 per month in missed billing. - The unsupported legacy system consumes engineering time and creates operational risk. - Customers need a reliable portal for invoices and credit card/ACH payments. - LanLine lacks efficient tracking for technician travel, on-site time, assets, maintenance dates, and proactive replacement opportunities. - Staff adoption and data quality remain critical dependencies for any new platform.

Rev.io can reduce billing from nearly a week toward one day by automating recurring charges and moving ticket labor, parts, and approvals into a controlled billing workflow. Mobile time tracking, travel/on-site timers, customer alerts, and permission-based status flows can improve technician accountability and capture billable work. The customer portal modernizes invoice delivery and payment collection. Asset and scheduled-maintenance tracking can support proactive replacement recommendations for UPS batteries, drives, firewalls, and other equipment. Real-time dashboards, collections automation, branded invoices, parent-child billing, and QuickBooks integration provide better operational control while preserving accounting workflows. Revy can improve grammar and customer-facing notes when technicians provide usable source detail

Epic Systems needs to replace a fragmented DTools + Slack workflow with a connected operating platform that can manage leads through project delivery and billing. DTools is not meeting the team’s needs for CRM, project management, mobile field execution, or mid-project material changes. The desired end state is Portal for proposal creation and Rev.io for CRM, project fulfillment, scheduling, technician work, invoicing, payments, and QuickBooks handoff.

Broken Relationship with a Rev.io Competitor

DTools project management is difficult and does not support the team’s real-world workflow well. Added or repriced materials during an active job are treated as change orders, creating friction in job costing and billing. DTools’ mobile experience is browser-based and considered unusable for leaders and field staff. Leads are tracked in Slack without a structured pipeline. The team also wants simple deposit and progress invoicing, centralized technician notes/photos, scheduling, time tracking, and reliable QuickBooks synchronization.

Rev.io can consolidate lead tracking, opportunities, project/ticket execution, dispatch, field time, billing, and reporting while Portal handles proposals and distributor pricing. Key value includes eliminating DTools and Slack, supporting enhancement/progress invoices for mid-project material changes, providing a native offline mobile app, improving field-to-office visibility, and syncing itemized invoices and customer/product data to QuickBooks. Revy can further reduce administrative effort by answering operational questions and creating records through conversational AI.

V2 Systems is a Boston-based commercial security integrator doing roughly $20–25M/year with 12–15 employees and growth potential toward 30. The company is still running core operations through QuickBooks Desktop, Excel templates, Google Calendar, manufacturer portals, third-party GPS, and manual office processes. Keith recognizes the need to professionalize operations so the business can scale, reduce paper/manual work, improve technician productivity, and capture more RMR margin directly.

Digital Transformation

- Tech field notes, parts used, time tracking, and job costing are handled through Excel templates and manual processes. - Scheduling is done in Google Calendar; GPS exists only through a third-party vehicle tool and is not tied to dispatch or billing. - Only two office staff support a large business, making manual RMR billing and admin work painful. - Quoting/pricing is difficult because distributor and manufacturer pricing is volatile and client-specific. - QuickBooks Desktop limits real-time workflow integration. - RMR is often billed by manufacturers, leaving V2 with referral commission instead of full margin.

Rev.io can create value by consolidating ticketing, dispatch, time tracking, mobile field notes, GPS, inventory, job costing, invoicing, and recurring billing into one operating platform. The biggest hard ROI is helping V2 bring RMR billing in-house; Keith estimated this could improve margins by roughly 20 points while still staying below MSRP. Rev.io also gives V2 a scalable process for projects, service work, and long-duration commercial jobs while reducing office burden.

Digital Transformation

- PercFab currently operates across several disconnected tools: Zoho for CRM and ticketing Google Calendar for dispatch and scheduling Google Sheets for MAC address tracking External tools and processes for quoting Rev.io for billing - Approximately 300 Verizon representatives can originate sales. Deal information arrives through email and triggers automated Zoho workflows that create accounts, opportunities, and templated Google Sheets. - Replicating this automated Verizon lead-intake process is the largest potential blocker to replacing Zoho. - MAC addresses are tracked separately in Google Sheets, creating manual work and limiting centralized asset reporting. - Provisioning remains manual, with the team entering customer information into Verizon’s portal after receiving porting forms. - Pricing will be a critical factor in the decision. - The team needs a deeper review of inventory management before determining overall fit.

- Use Rev.io’s shared database architecture to add PSA functionality without syncing or duplicating existing billing, customer, product, and recurring-service data. - Consolidate lead management, opportunities, quoting, e-signature, ticketing, dispatch, inventory, reporting, and billing into one platform. - Automate the conversion of accepted quotes into recurring services and implementation tickets. - Replace Google Calendar with an integrated dispatch board for scheduling installations and service work. - Move MAC address and device tracking from spreadsheets into centralized inventory and asset records. - Use Revii AI and BI reporting to retrieve asset information, generate MAC address reports, create tickets, and reduce administrative effort. - Give field technicians mobile access to tickets, notes, schedules, time entry, quoting, and customer information. - Reduce duplicate entry and improve visibility from the initial Verizon lead through installation and recurring billing.

Crown Networks is re-evaluating PSA options after previously passing on Rev.io because project management was not mature enough at the time. They currently use ConnectWise and have spent almost two years getting it functional, but it remains clunky, time-consuming, and difficult to fully adopt. Crown does a lot of project-based work, relies heavily on subcontractors, and needs a better way to manage quoting, project execution, work orders, billing, payments, and QuickBooks Online sync without data living across Word, Excel, PDFs, OneDrive, and ConnectWise.

Broken Relationship with a Rev.io Competitor

ConnectWise took significant time and cost to onboard, and Crown has not fully recouped that investment. Project managers only partially use ConnectWise for projects because it is too clunky, so they create detailed work orders in Word, track project details in Excel, and store information across OneDrive/file servers. Most work goes to subcontractors, but licensing 160 subcontractors does not make sense. WiseSync/WisePay was recently added for QuickBooks sync and payment surcharging, but Ron said it is still clunky and creates invoice sync errors accounting has to fix.

Rev.io can give Crown a more modern, easier-to-use PSA that better supports project-heavy work without relying on disconnected Word docs, Excel sheets, PDFs, and manual processes. The biggest value is simplifying project management and quote-to-project workflow while reducing administrative friction around invoicing, payments, QuickBooks sync, and vendor cost tracking. If Rev.io can prove onboarding is lighter and the platform is easier to configure than ConnectWise, Crown could avoid another year of frustration and move to a system that better fits their project/subcontractor-heavy model.

The business needs to determine whether consolidating onto Rev.io will simplify operations

Single Points of Failure across employee resources

- ConnectWise inventory is poorly maintained and not trusted; the immediate need is selective control of valuable and serialized equipment such as physical phones. - The company uses roughly four separate ConnectWise agreements for billing, hosted coverage, SIP trunks, and maintenance, creating administrative fragmentation. - Managed-services and telecom billing are split between ConnectWise/Alternative Payments and Rev.io, preventing a unified customer experience. - Alternative Payments costs $999 per month before transaction economics are considered. - ConnectWise ticket history and configuration must be migrated safely, and the team wants credible references from other ConnectWise conversions

Copeland wants to grow without adding headcount at the same rate. Its seven-to-eight-person team supports roughly 3,000–4,000 NinjaOne seats, but ConnectWise creates rigid, click-heavy work across service, billing, reporting, collections, and account management. The platform costs about $30,000 per month and renews in mid-2027, creating a defined window to evaluate a replacement. Copeland needs an automation-first PSA that preserves its human-touch, agile operating style while improving scalability, visibility, and employee leverage.

Single Points of Failure across employee resources

- Monthly billing consumes 10–12 hours from a key employee due to WisePay, ConnectWise, and QuickBooks reconciliation. - Pax8 billing and contract data do not align reliably. - Collections are manual, and the bookkeeper lacks sufficient visibility. - BrightGauge reporting is static and requires manual exports and table maintenance. - Account managers manually log activities, time, and follow-ups after calls. - ConnectWise workflows are rigid, procedural, and poorly matched to Copeland’s culture. - Support and account management relationships have deteriorated. - Every additional capability requires another paid module. - Documentation/configuration integrations remain an evaluation concern

Rev.io can help Copeland scale its existing team through native AI, automation, and unified workflows. Revy can answer operational questions, summarize tickets, prepare QBRs, create records, capture notes, and schedule repeatable skills—while keeping actions permission-based and human-approved. Rev.io can reduce billing reconciliation by managing invoices, payments, credits, and reversals before pushing detail to QuickBooks. Native collections, Pax8 and NinjaOne integrations, ticketing, CRM, quoting, projects, mobile time capture, SQL-level analytics, and Signal & Send can replace manual work and paid add-ons. The strongest value case is reclaimed staff time, improved account coverage, faster decisions, and growth without proportional hiring

Pioneer Telecom is re-evaluating Rev.io as it works to grow and separate the telecom business from other Pioneer entities. The immediate driver is reducing manual tax calculation, reporting, and billing work across SkySwitch, Cordial, and White Label carrier services. Anna currently handles billing in QuickBooks while referencing SureTax codes manually, and their accountant is involved in tax handling. They need a clearer AR/billing system of record that can automate tax calculations, usage rating, reporting, payments, and collections.

Single Points of Failure across employee resources

- Tax calculations, tax-code updates, and reports for filing/remittance are handled manually today. - QuickBooks is being used as the billing/invoicing/payment experience, but it is not purpose-built for telecom taxation or multi-carrier usage billing. - Pioneer uses multiple carriers — SkySwitch, Cordial, and White Label — so the lower-cost SkySwitch-only Rev.io version may not support the full use case. - Payment processing currently runs through Slice, creating potential migration and customer-payment workflow considerations. - Compliance partner outreach previously stalled, leaving tax filing/remittance ownership unresolved. - Pricing has increased from the prior quote, and Anna flagged that management needs to review the cost.

Rev.io can consolidate multi-carrier billing into one platform, automate SkySwitch/Cordial/White Label CDR imports, include a wholesale SureTax license, calculate taxes automatically, generate reports needed for filing/remittance, and push reconciled AR data into QuickBooks. Rev.io also provides a customer portal, ACH/credit card auto-pay, collections automation, payment processing options, and a path to compliance partner referrals. This reduces manual tax and billing work while giving Pioneer a scalable billing foundation for telecom growth.

Data Network Systems needs a way to expand and bill non-telephony revenue streams without Rev.io’s percentage-based billing model eroding margin on low-margin circuits, recurring packages, and federal/non-telephony services. Today, Rev.io is mainly being used for CDR rating while QuickBooks and other tools handle much of the broader business, creating a split operating model.

Single Points of Failure across employee resources

- Approximately 80% of the business cannot be run through Rev.io under the current percentage-fee economics. - Low-margin circuits and monthly recurring packages are especially sensitive; a $1,200 circuit with $100–$150 margin becomes unattractive if percentage fees consume too much profit. - Some billing-package clients are not in Rev.io at all due to cost concerns, limiting system-of-record completeness. - They previously tried Rev.io help desk but discontinued because billing became a cost center when zero-cost items were added. - Current stack is fragmented across QuickBooks, Rev.io, Open Project, Salesforce, and partner tools. - Growth is increasingly non-telephony, so the current Rev.io-only-for-CDR model does not support where the business is going.

Rev.io PSA can create a path for Data Network Systems to keep Rev.io as the telecom/CDR billing engine while using PSA for projects, service ticketing, dispatch, recurring charges, one-off charges, and non-telephony billing without applying the same percentage-based fee structure that is blocking adoption. Because PSA and billing share customer/product data, the prospect could consolidate operational workflows, quote and bill from one customer record, and potentially present combined invoices while protecting margin on circuits and services.

Preparing for Rapid Growth

- Limited SkySwitch/Rev.io access restricts products, reports, billing profiles, templates, and visibility. - Current billing flow still requires manual usage aggregation, tax work, CloudOlive reconciliation, and ConnectWise updates. - Prior API/integration attempts failed due to data volume and mapping complexity. - Business Central integration timing needs confirmation. - CloudOlive and ConnectBooster replacement depend on vendor coverage, economics, and integration fit. - ConnectWise agreement/addition mapping and product catalog alignment must be validated. - Full PSA replacement is not assumed yet; Halo remains a possible alternative.

New York Security Solutions is re-evaluating Rev.io after a prior evaluation because several required capabilities have since been released. They are running a fragmented workflow across DTools for quoting/estimates, Halo PSA for ticketing, QuickBooks Online for accounting/invoicing, PandaDocs for proposals/contracts, Box for file sharing, and SiteOwl for installed inventory/job-walk documentation. The largest operational issue is the DTools-to-QBO handoff: invoices push as one summary line instead of itemized hardware, labor, recurring, and deposit lines, forcing finance to invoice out of QBO

Broken Relationship with a Rev.io Competitor

DTools is strong for quoting but weak post-sale. Finance hates the accounting workflow because QBO does not receive the invoice detail they need. Recurring revenue is difficult to manage: licenses, MSAs, and leases are billed from QBO, vendor cost increases require manual updates across customer records, and recurring profitability is hard to see. Customer portal needs are broader than current state: quotes/approvals, renewals, and project dashboards. They also need better help desk/field ticketing, mobile access for sales/project management, file storage, distributor integrations, and confidence that DTools data can migrate correctly.

Rev.io can create value by consolidating post-sale operations into one source of truth: itemized invoicing and payments with QBO, ticketing/help desk with SLAs, dispatch, customer portal, recurring agreements, MRR/profitability reporting, projects, inventory, assets, and mobile access. The biggest value driver is eliminating duplicate finance work and enabling invoices to flow to QBO with the right detail. Additional value comes from replacing Halo PSA, potentially reducing PandaDocs/Box reliance, improving recurring revenue management with mass updates, and giving customers better visibility through portal/shared dashboards.

B&S Integrated is re-evaluating Rev.io as a consolidated operating platform before its FieldPulse contract expires in October/November. The company is a Northeast security integrator with ~13 employees serving government contractors, security systems, fire alarms, inspections, monitoring, construction projects, service/maintenance agreements, and multi-year product licenses. Current workflows are split across FieldPulse, QuickBooks Online, and separate project management processes, creating gaps in job costing, inventory, field time capture, invoicing, dashboards, and service visibility.

Broken Relationship with a Rev.io Competitor

- FieldPulse is useful for scheduling but limited for full project lifecycle management, procurement, contract process, milestones, and profitability tracking. - No reliable centralized job costing; labor hours are difficult to capture because technicians do not consistently clock in/out. - QuickBooks and FieldPulse inventory are inaccurate; serialized inventory and truck stock are not well controlled, and items may be missed on invoices. - Office staff must manually add labor/items before invoicing because field activity does not flow cleanly to invoices. - Reporting is weak; dashboards do not clearly show new/unassigned jobs, technician utilization, service desk status, or project profitability. - Customer ticket intake is manual through calls/web forms; FieldPulse portal exists but is not adopted. - Progress billing is manual and retainage requires a separate QuickBooks invoice.

Rev.io can create value by consolidating quoting, service delivery, project management, scheduling, inventory, procurement, field workflows, invoicing, recurring billing, and reporting into one operating platform. Key value drivers include job costing, project/milestone invoicing, technician mobile time tracking that converts to billable labor, truck stock pulls that flow to jobs/invoices, serialized and multi-location inventory, email-to-ticket automation, QuickBooks Online integration, recurring inspection scheduling, CMS account/contact sync, and Revy AI reporting/dashboard creation.
